:::{#thm-wlln}
#### Weak law of large numbers

Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be [IID](independence.qmd#def-iid) random variables
with mean $\mean$ and finite variance $\ss > 0$,
and let $\bar X_n \eqdef \avgin X_i$ be the sample mean.
Then the sample mean [converges in probability](#def-convergence-in-probability) to $\mean$:

$$
\bar X_n \inprob \mean
$$

:::

::: proof

By @cor-sum-iid-moments, $\E{S_n} = n\mean$ and $\Var{S_n} = n\ss$,
where $S_n \eqdef \sumin X_i$, so $\bar X_n = S_n / n$ has

$$
\ba
\E{\bar X_n}
&= \frac{1}{n}\E{S_n}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n} \cdot n\mean
&& \text{(mean of a sum of IID variables)}\\
&= \mean
&& \text{(cancel $n$)}\\
\Var{\bar X_n}
&= \frac{1}{n^2}\Var{S_n}
&& \text{(variance of a constant multiple)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n^2} \cdot n\ss
&& \text{(variance of a sum of IID variables)}\\
&= \frac{\ss}{n}
&& \text{(cancel one factor of $n$)}
\ea
$$

Fix $\varepsilon > 0$ and let $k \eqdef \varepsilon \sqrt{n} / \sdpar$,
so that $k \sdpar / \sqrt{n} = \varepsilon$.
[Chebyshev's inequality](#thm-chebyshev) for $\bar X_n$,
whose standard deviation is $\sdpar / \sqrt{n}$, gives

$$
\ba
0 \le \Prf{\abs{\bar X_n - \mean} \ge \varepsilon}
&= \Prf{\abs{\bar X_n - \mean} \ge k \frac{\sdpar}{\sqrt{n}}}
&& \text{(definition of $k$)}\\
&\le \frac{1}{k^2}
&& \text{(Chebyshev's inequality)}\\
&= \frac{\ss}{n \varepsilon^2}
&& \text{(substitute $k$)}
\ea
$$

The bound goes to zero as $n \to \infty$,
so the probability, squeezed between zero and the bound, goes to zero.
This holds for every $\varepsilon > 0$.

:::
